faqs.q: A snake turned up at my Chesapeake home — what happens next?
faqs.a: Call us and keep people and pets clear until we identify it. Most Chesapeake snake calls are harmless rat snakes, racers, or garter snakes, and the eastern copperhead — venomous and found statewide — is the one to treat with real caution. Snakes are the one class Virginia allows a permit holder to move a short distance: same or neighboring county or city, suitable habitat, with the release-site landowner's written permission, and we report the move to DWR. We never kill a snake as a marketed service.

Chesapeake.wildlife_intro:
Chesapeake sprawls from South Norfolk's older blocks to swamp-edge subdivisions where snakes, raccoons, and bats are routine in Chesapeake. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: great Dismal Swamp's eastern edge, Elizabeth River South Branch, Intracoastal Waterway and canal woods. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Chesapeake — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
